script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Good morning! I'm Dr. Martinez. I understand your little one has been having a fever?

script.speaker: parent
script.text: Yes, she started running a fever two days ago and I'm really worried. This is my first baby and I don't know if I should have brought her in sooner.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: You absolutely did the right thing bringing her in. Fever in babies this young is always something we want to evaluate. Can you tell me what her temperature has been?

script.speaker: parent
script.text: It's been between 101 and 102.5. I've been checking it constantly with the ear thermometer. Is that too high?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: For a 6-month-old, any fever over 100.4 is concerning. How has she been acting otherwise? Eating, sleeping, wet diapers?

script.speaker: parent
script.text: She's been so fussy and clingy. Her appetite is definitely down - she's only taking about half her normal bottles. [baby fussing]

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: I can hear she's not feeling well. What about wet diapers? Has she been having normal wet diapers?

script.speaker: parent
script.text: Maybe a little less than usual? I've been counting them like you're supposed to, but I think it's been fewer.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Good job keeping track. Any vomiting, diarrhea, or changes in her stool?

script.speaker: parent
script.text: No vomiting, but her poop has been a little looser than normal. Not quite diarrhea though.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Has she had any cough, runny nose, or seem to have trouble breathing?

script.speaker: parent
script.text: No cough or runny nose. Her breathing seems okay, but she's been breathing a little faster when the fever is high.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: That's very observant of you. Any rash anywhere on her body?

script.speaker: parent
script.text: I don't think so. I've been checking her all over. Should I be looking for something specific?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: You're doing great. Let me examine her now. Has she had any medications or vaccines recently?

script.speaker: parent
script.text: She had her 4-month shots about 6 weeks ago. I gave her some infant Tylenol yesterday when her fever was really high.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: [examining] Good, and how much Tylenol did you give her? Let me listen to her chest first.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: The package said 2.5 milliliters for her weight. Was that right? [baby crying]

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: [examining] That sounds about right for her size. Her lungs sound clear. Now let me check her ears and throat.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: She hates having her ears looked at. Is she going to be okay?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: [examining] I know it's uncomfortable for her. Her ears look good, no infection there. Let me feel her belly and check her fontanelle.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: What's a fontanelle? Her soft spot? Is something wrong with it?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: [examining] The fontanelle is her soft spot, and it looks normal - not sunken or bulging. Her belly feels fine too. Let me take her temperature.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: It was 101.8 about an hour ago. Has it gotten worse?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: It's 102.1 now. Given her age and the fever pattern, I'd like to run some tests to make sure there's no serious infection.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: Tests? What kind of tests? Is she really sick?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: For babies under 3 months, we're very cautious with fever, but even at 6 months, we want to be thorough. I'd like to get some blood work and a urine sample.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: How do you get urine from a baby? Will the blood test hurt her?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: We'll use a special bag for the urine, and the blood draw is just a small poke. Most babies cry for just a moment. This will help us rule out any bacterial infections.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: Okay, if you think it's necessary. What happens after the tests?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: We should have results in about an hour. In the meantime, you can continue the Tylenol every 6 hours, and we'll keep her comfortable here.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: Should I be giving her anything else? More fluids? I feel so helpless.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: You're doing everything right. Keep offering her bottles frequently, even small amounts. If the tests are normal, this is likely just a viral infection that will resolve on its own.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: How long do these things usually last? When should I worry?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Viral fevers typically last 3-5 days. Bring her back if the fever goes above 103, if she becomes very lethargic, or stops having wet diapers. But let's see what these tests show first.
